**1. The question is always saved.** Before anything is sent to me, `save_ask` in `src/hidden_anchor.rs:272` writes the question to `.suspense/asks/<unix-time>-<anchor>.pi`. That file holds what you typed, `mode: ask` and the system prompt. It's written even if the anchor can't be resolved: the question goes under a new random anchor with the error recorded beside it (`src/prompt_mode.rs:1258`). Questions go in `asks/`, not `history/`, so they don't show up in your prompt history.

**2. The response is logged too, but only with your uncommitted changes.** In the current working tree, `AskLog` (`src/prompt_mode.rs:578`) saves a `.json` file next to the `.pi` when the run ends. It uses the same format as history entries: the compiled prompt I received, my output line by line, and any error. It also saves if you close or replace the question partway through. The last commit (`e25188e`) doesn't have `AskLog`, so a build from that commit only saves the question. There are no `.json` files in `.suspense/asks/` yet, which suggests the app you're running doesn't have this change yet. It might also just mean no run has finished since you built it.

**Git:** `.gitignore` only excludes `harness.json`, `queue/` and the draft, so `.suspense/asks/` isn't ignored. Some of the older questions are already committed, so anything you ask there will be committed and pushed with the repo unless you add `/.suspense/asks/` to `.gitignore`.

Separately, Claude Code also keeps its own copy of this conversation under `~/.claude/projects/`, whatever the app does.
